questions.text: What is "routing" in Laravel?
options: The process of directing an incoming request to a specific controller method
questions.explanation: Routing directs an incoming request to a specific controller method.

questions.text: By default, where are web routes defined?
questions.explanation: Web routes are defined in routes/web.php.

questions.text: By default, where are API routes defined?
questions.explanation: API routes are defined in routes/api.php. (Since Laravel 11 this file is no longer created by default — php artisan install:api generates it — but it is still where API routes go.)

questions.text: Which HTTP verb is used to request/retrieve a resource or list of resources?
questions.explanation: GET retrieves data.

questions.text: Which HTTP verb is used to create a resource or submit data?
questions.explanation: POST creates a resource or submits data.

questions.text: Which HTTP verb overwrites a resource entirely / fully updates data?
questions.explanation: PUT overwrites a resource or updates data.

questions.text: Which HTTP verb is used to partially modify or update a resource?
questions.explanation: PATCH modifies/partially updates a resource.

questions.text: Which HTTP verb deletes a resource?
questions.explanation: DELETE removes a resource.

questions.text: What Laravel feature lets you generate URLs or redirects for a specific route easily, using ->name()?
questions.explanation: Named routes let you reference a route by name to build URLs/redirects.

questions.text: How do route parameters appear inside a route URI?
questions.explanation: Laravel route parameters are wrapped in curly braces, e.g. {id}.

questions.text: How do you make a route parameter optional?
options: Add a ! after the name, e.g. {name!}
Add a ? after the name, e.g. {name?}, and give the closure a default value
Wrap it in double braces, e.g. {{name}}
questions.explanation: Optional parameters use {name?} with a default value in the closure.

questions.text: Which method constrains the format of a route parameter using a regular expression?
questions.explanation: The where() method accepts a parameter name and a regex to constrain it.

questions.text: What is the purpose of a fallback route (Route::fallback())?
options: It runs before every other route
It catches requests not handled by any previously defined route, and should be placed last
It only works for POST requests
questions.explanation: Route::fallback() should be placed at the end to catch unhandled requests.

questions.text: Which Artisan command caches routes for a faster application load time in production?
questions.explanation: php artisan route:cache caches the routes.

questions.text: Complete the route definition so it responds to a GET request:
questions.explanation: Route::get() defines a route that responds to a GET request.

questions.text: Complete the route parameter syntax so $id is captured from the URL:
questions.explanation: Route parameters are written as {id} inside the URI string.

questions.text: Complete the Artisan command that clears the cached routes:
questions.explanation: php artisan route:clear clears the route cache.

questions.text: Complete the method call that constrains the id parameter to digits only:
questions.explanation: ->where('id', '[0-9]+') constrains the parameter with a regex.
